paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples with a larger number of examples
model_annotation: The diagram compares the performance of two example selection strategies, labeled “ST-ES” and “Random,” plotted against the number of in-context examples, ranging from 0 to 15 on a linear scale with integer tick marks. The y-axis represents the minimum ADE₂₀ (in units of distance), scaled linearly from 0.58 to 0.66, with tick marks at regular intervals of 0.02. The “ST-ES” strategy is depicted by a blue line with circular markers and a solid line, starting at a value of 0.66 at 0 examples and decreasing to 0.58 at 15 examples, with a sharp initial drop followed by a gradual decline and minor fluctuations. The “Random” strategy is shown by an orange line with circular markers and a solid line, beginning at 0.64 at 0 examples and remaining relatively stable around 0.63–0.64 for the entire range, with minor fluctuations but no significant trend or drop.

model_annotations.English: This line plot compares the performance of two example selection strategies—ST-ES and Random—as measured by minADE₂₀ (in units of length, likely meters) across varying numbers of in-context examples, ranging from 0 to 15. The x-axis, labeled "Number of Examples," is linear and spans from 0 to 15, with tick marks appearing at regular intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled "minADE₂₀ (←)", is also linear and ranges from 0.58 to 0.66. The ST-ES strategy is represented by a blue line with circular markers and a solid line style; it begins at a high value of approximately 0.66 at 0 examples, then rapidly decreases to a minimum of about 0.58 at 2 examples, and remains relatively stable at that level until the end of the range at 15 examples, where it settles at approximately 0.58. The Random strategy is represented by an orange line with square markers and a solid line style; it starts at approximately 0.64 at 0 examples, fluctuates slightly downward and upward, and stabilizes around a value of approximately 0.63 from 5 to 15 examples.
